title: LeForge Message
description: The unit of work that crosses a channel. The six top-level fields are the stable public envelope (server/internal/domain/message.go). Everything else travels in metadata under the well-known keys documented below; unknown metadata keys are user data and are carried through untouched.

id.description: Sortable unique id: 'msg_' + base36 millisecond timestamp + 20 hex chars. Consumers deduplicate on it.

type.description: Message type used for routing (channel 'types' filters, 'when' conditions). Dotted names by convention.

source.description: Producing node id, or 'external:<actor>' for messages injected through the API. Empty only for legacy producers.

target.description: Optional node id the producer wants the message routed toward (dynamic routing). Empty means 'route by channel rules'.

payload.description: Arbitrary JSON. Agents emit JSON objects; injected messages default to {}.

metadata.description: Routing, lineage and tracing data. Keys set by the platform cannot be overridden through Emit.metadata or injection metadata.

graph_version.description: Graph version that produced the message.

channel.description: Channel id the message was published on (set per copy).

correlation_id.description: Stable id of the whole workflow; the id of the first message of the chain.

causation_id.description: Id of the input message whose turn emitted this one.

hops.description: Agent hops so far; messages over spec.maxHops (default 64) are dropped (cycle guard).

injected_by.description: Authenticated identity that injected the message through the API.

attempt.description: Reserved for consumer-side delivery attempt bookkeeping.

replica.description: Replica index of the producing node.

held_for.description: Approval id while the message waits at a human gate.

edited_by.description: Approver who replaced the payload when releasing a held message.
